guide.q.what_is_catalog_transfer: Can I copy a listing or group to another site?
guide.a.what_is_catalog_transfer: Yes. Any listing or group can be saved as one file, then loaded into this or another site to re-create it — with its prices, group memberships, package settings and parent links. It is the quick way to move a listing between sites, or to keep a spare copy. The file is the same either way: what you save is exactly what a load accepts.
guide.q.how_do_i_export_catalog: How do I save a listing or group?
guide.a.how_do_i_export_catalog:
Open the listing's Actions tab (or a group's detail page) and choose Export. You download a .json file named after the listing or group.

Editors do not see the webhook address in their copies, because that field is hidden from them everywhere.
guide.q.how_do_i_import_catalog: How do I load a listing or group?
guide.a.how_do_i_import_catalog:
Go to Listings or Groups and choose Import, then upload the file. The file's kind says whether a listing or a group is created.

Any parent listings and groups it names must already exist here, and the incoming name cannot match an existing listing or group. If anything is wrong, the page tells you exactly which field.

Import is switched off in demo mode.
guide.a.what_is_in_catalog_file:
The file carries what you sell, and nothing else: the structure and the pricing. Everything is joined by name, never by number, because names survive a move between sites and numbers do not.

Pictures, file attachments, attendees, and any money or booking history are left out on purpose — a copy describes what you sell, not the records tied to one site. The file carries a version number, so a file from a different version is refused rather than loaded wrongly.
